correctness.rationale: The precise Schur interval (-1/2,1), stationary augmented Lyapunov equation and rational stationary variance are derived. Two exact algebraic factorizations establish global wrong-sign exclusion and the strict 1/9 bound. A uniform boundary-layer expansion together with two-sided compactness of every minimizer proves the sharp sqrt(1+q) tuning and risk law. Actual verify.py was executed successfully using symbolic Lyapunov elimination, identity checks, derivatives, singular expansion and exact rational cases. Results need no Gaussian assumption, only independent finite-variance innovations. No finite computation is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The focal 2023 primary work characterizes stationary heavy-ball fluctuations for finite-epoch anticorrelated noise and restricts nonnegative momentum; its explicit variance relations do not state the AR(1) full-sign classification or one-ninth optimally tuned boundary layer. The checked 2024 stochastic-heavy-ball works concern independent noise or minibatch tuning. The 2021 two-buffer positive-negative momentum method is a distinct algorithm. Published semantic search and the accessible deduplication claims yielded no implication-equivalent claim; specialized classical ARMA/control theory remains a residual publication-precedence risk.
residual_risks: A pre-existing AR(1) stochastic heavy-ball/H2 filter-design result could implicitly state the same optimal momentum sign or singular ratio under different control-theory terminology; publication precedence is not independently resolved.
Only passages relevant to the precise comparison were inspected in several long primary texts; lack of an identified match is not a universal whole-corpus absence claim.
The AR(1) benchmark is not exactly the without-replacement epoch noise process of the primary motivating paper.

value.rationale: The work resolves a natural tunable sign question that arises when gradient noise is temporally correlated: a globally wrong-sign choice always increases last-iterate stationary risk, whereas the opposite sign can reduce it. A nontrivial sharp endpoint variational analysis shows optimally tuned momentum yields an asymptotic ninefold variance reduction at extreme antipersistence and gives the sqrt tuning scale. These are structural and calibrated design facts beyond a single numeric example; no broader empirical applicability is asserted.
